aggregate_metrics.ADPR_denominator: All dependency_points unless a paper section explicitly reports primary_async_dependency_ids only.
aggregate_metrics.minimum_success_condition_for_task_level: The primary_async_dependency_id passes in the final integrated workspace.

annotation_notes: The Unicode-version to width dependency is the primary async signal because the width worker can implement _wcmatch_version against stale assumptions about list_versions ordering, string format, and latest/lowest supported values.
The width algorithm integration dependency records public width behavior that should be measured after the version catalog and algorithm artifacts are combined.
The version local probe group is not perfectly isolated because tests/test_ucslevel.py also exercises _wcmatch_version(); this limitation is already recorded in the quality record.
These labels identify public test-observable contracts and implicated files, not solution code.

dependency_points.contract_summary: The width algorithm must consume list_versions() as an ascending catalog of supported Unicode version strings and implement exact, nearest, low, high, latest, and invalid-version matching against that catalog.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when version-catalog/latest probes and nearest-version matching probes pass in the integrated workspace.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The width worker may hard-code a stale supported-version list or assume a different ordering/string format, causing _wcmatch_version failures once the completed version catalog is integrated.

dependency_points.contract_summary: The completed width algorithm must preserve public wcwidth() and wcswidth() behavior for empty strings, C0 controls, combining characters, East-Asian wide characters, emoji ZWJ sequences, VS-16 presentation, and table integrity.
dependency_points.resolution_criteria: Resolved when version-matching and public width-behavior probes pass in the final integrated workspace.
dependency_points.stale_failure_mode: The width artifact may pass a narrow version-matching slice while leaving public width semantics inconsistent with table data and emoji handling in the integrated evaluator.

evaluation_checkpoint_policy.minimum_policy: Run probe tests after each agent final artifact and after final integration.
evaluation_checkpoint_policy.recommended_policy: Run probe tests after every committed patch, every explicit artifact transfer, and final integration.

ADPR.definition: Fraction of registered dependency_points whose required integrated_probe_tests pass in the final integrated workspace.
ADPR.name: Async Dependency Pass Rate

CAIL.definition: downstream_resolution_step minus upstream_resolution_step when both probe groups have been evaluated.
CAIL.name: Cross-Agent Integration Lag

DRS.definition: First recorded checkpoint at which all required integrated_probe_tests for a dependency point pass.
DRS.name: Dependency Resolution Step

SAD.definition: Interval during which a downstream worker acts on a contract assumption inconsistent with the latest upstream artifact visible in the integrated history.
SAD.name: Stale Assumption Duration

purpose: Dependency-level labels for measuring whether asynchronous multi-agent coding resolves wcwidth's Unicode-version catalog and terminal-width algorithm contracts promptly.
